texts.li: It's the shortest night of the year, and {A_nameDef} wants a bonfire: a proper one, taller than the roof, with singing and too much drink and nobody on the night shift.\n\nIt would burn through a good stack of firewood.
Midsummer. {A_nameDef} has been stacking logs behind the barn for a week and has finally asked the council: can we light it?

li.label: Light the bonfire
li.outcome: The midsummer fire burned until dawn. Nobody remembers going to bed.

li.label: Not this year: we need the wood
li.outcome: No bonfire. {A_nameDef} sat on the log pile all evening, looking at it.

li.label: A small fire, no drinking
li.outcome: A modest fire, early to bed. Pleasant enough. {A_nameDef} calls it "a candle with ambitions".

texts.li: The last of the crops are in. {A_nameDef}, who planted most of them, wants a harvest supper: a proper one, the kind with second helpings. It would cost about {COUNT} raw food.\n\nWinter is coming either way.

{A_nameDef} has spent the whole season in the fields and is asking for one night to celebrate it: a harvest home, about {COUNT} raw food's worth. "We grew it," {A_nameDef} says. "We should get to taste it."

li.label: A harvest feast for everyone
li.outcome: The harvest home was a triumph. Even the cook had seconds.

li.label: Store every scrap for winter
li.outcome: Every grain went into storage. Sensible. {A_nameDef} is not speaking to the council.

li.label: A modest supper
li.outcome: A good meal, nothing extravagant. The storeroom barely noticed.

texts.li: The longest night of the year. Dark by mid-afternoon, cold enough to crack teeth. {A_nameDef} thinks the colony should mark it somehow, the way people did back home: extra food, a long evening by the fire.
{A_nameDef} found everyone huddled in separate corners last night, staring at the walls. "It's midwinter," {A_nameDef} told the council. "We should be together for it."

li.label: Extra rations for the long night
li.outcome: Full bellies on the longest night. Someone sang. Nobody stopped them.

li.label: Stories by the fire, no feast
li.outcome: A long evening of stories by the fire. Some were sad, some were filthy, all of them were better than the silence.

li.label: Just another night
li.outcome: The longest night passed like any other: cold, dark and quiet.

ColonyCouncil.DilemmaDef.label: naming the year

texts.li: Somebody started it as a joke: the new year needs a name. Now the whole colony is arguing about it. {A_nameDef} has proposed "the year of {A_nameDef}", loudly and often.\n\nThe council has been asked to settle it before someone gets hurt.

The annals need a name for the new year, apparently. {A_nameDef} has volunteered {A_possessive} own, with a straight face. Others have suggested naming it for those we've lost. One person has suggested the muffalo.

ColonyCouncil.DilemmaDef.traditionLabel: naming the year after a muffalo

li.label: The year of {A_nameDef}
li.outcome: This is now officially the year of {A_nameDef}. {A_nameDef} has mentioned it a dozen times since breakfast.

li.label: Name it for those we lost
li.outcome: The year carries the names of the dead. Nobody argued with that.

li.label: The year of the muffalo
li.outcome: It is the year of the muffalo. The muffalo has not been informed. {A_nameDef} is sulking.

texts.li: The raiders left plenty behind: boots, coats, a rifle that's almost clean. {A_nameDef} did most of the shooting and thinks that earns first pick.\n\nNot everyone agrees.
The bodies are still warm, and the argument over their gear has already started. {A_nameDef}, who killed three of them, has claimed the best of it.

li.label: {A_nameDef} earned first pick
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} took the best of the spoils. Some of the others are counting who fought and who hid.

li.label: Everything goes to the stores, shared equally
li.outcome: The spoils went to the common stores. Fair, and everybody knows it. {A_nameDef} knows it loudest.

li.label: The fighters get the spoils
li.outcome: Everyone who fought got a share. Those who stayed inside got the dishes.

texts.li: The raiders lie where they fell. {A_nameDef} asks what the council wants done with them: graves, a pyre, or the treeline and the scavengers.\n\nEveryone has an opinion, and none of them are quiet.
{A_nameDef} has been staring at the bodies outside the wall for an hour. "They were people," {A_nameDef} says. "Somebody's people. What do we do with them?"

li.label: Give them graves
li.outcome: The raiders got graves at the edge of the colony. It took most of a day. The kind-hearted slept better for it.

li.label: Burn them
li.outcome: The pyre burned all night. Quick and clean, mostly. Someone watched it far too closely.

li.label: Drag them to the treeline
li.outcome: The bodies went to the treeline. The scavengers came at dusk, and everyone heard them.

texts.li: We're alive. Everyone left standing is grinning like an idiot, and {A_nameDef} wants to celebrate it properly: a victory feast, tonight, about {COUNT} raw food.\n\nThe repairs can wait until morning. Can't they?
The shooting stopped an hour ago. {A_nameDef} is already asking the council for a feast. "We earned it," {A_nameDef} says, wiping someone else's blood off {A_possessive} sleeve.

li.label: A victory feast
li.outcome: They feasted like people who'd just survived something, because they had.

li.label: Repairs first, celebrations later
li.outcome: Straight back to work: walls, wounds and bodies. The celebration never quite happened.
